summary: The loader variant loader-diag-xnu-rx-md1 for the NAT-078 delivery run: asserted hunks turn the pinned NAT-074 big-window loader sources and the NAT-076 bulk-OUT engine into a loader that, after layout and before the kernel jump, receives the padded root image over USB bulk-OUT directly into the md1 reserve (2,475,720,704 B) with a bounded receive phase (cap 240 s, pet every 30 s, final pet before the jump), a CPU self-test of eight pages of the reserve before the destination is installed, and delivery counters in the loader log; the NAT-077 hash probe is its md0 PID 1 (--ramdisk). Built (build-003), packaged by the NAT-044 chain (package-002, RECOVERY SHA-256 d9502498...02ef), 110 host tests (90 with the compiled loader code in Unicorn, 20 end-to-end with the real sender on the NAT-076 model), a mutation pass of 580 candidates (486 killed, 91 do not build, 3 survivors, each shown to be equivalent), and a decision template for NAT-078. Nothing was run on the phone.

acceptance.1_hunks: make_variant79.py applies counted, asserted hunks to a copy of the pinned NAT-074 loader source and the NAT-076 engine; a missing or duplicated anchor is an error naming the hunk and writes nothing (test_every_hunk_matches_exactly_once_in_the_real_nat074_sources, test_a_missing_anchor_*, test_a_duplicated_anchor_*); the source headers are copied byte for byte and the base SHAs (artifacts/nat-079/build-003/build.json, which also records the SHA-256 of every file of the NAT-076 engine and of the pinned sources) and the licences (GPL-2.0 for the loader and the vendor DWC3 code) are recorded in the build record and the README; only docs/procedures/nat-079 and artifacts/nat-079 were written; the NAT-074/NAT-076 sources are read, not edited.
acceptance.2_host_tests: test_nat079.py runs the compiled receive phase in Unicorn: it ends on rx_bytes == rx_size (done), on the cap (timeout) and on a failed self-test (status 5, no destination is installed; a host that sent before the destination was real is refused without touching the reserve); the watchdog is petted every 30 s through the whole phase and a phase that overruns the deadline is stopped by the NAT-044 reset sequence with the pets unchanged; the reserve handed to the phase is the loader's own md1 reserve (16 KiB aligned, inside the 4 GiB window, outside the clear plan) for the built payload; the binary rules of NAT-074 still hold (one s5e_wdt_pet call in the image, reached only from the tick and the final pet; the guard arms once for 83 s and never pets or disarms; no cache maintenance in the new code; no vector or float registers). test_e2e79.py runs the same phase against the NAT-076 model with the real tools/ios/root_send.py sender.
acceptance.3_package_template_mutation: The image is packaged by the NAT-044 chain (package-002, hashes pinned in artifacts/nat-079/package-002/package.json and recomputed from the file); docs/procedures/nat-079/decision-template-nat078.md names Image.payload (95aec19a...0512) and RECOVERY (d9502498...02ef) and the NAT-080 hashes; the mutation pass (docs/procedures/nat-079/mutation.json) lists three survivors with reasons in equivalent.json. No native run.

findings: DONE means committed, not verified: the loader counts the bytes the engine accepted; the digest is checked by the PID 1 probe (NAT-077) reading /dev/rmd1.

Direct DMA into the reserve was chosen over the staged copy that NAT-076 made the default: the loader runs with the MMU off and the staged copy is a byte-granular loop; this is an engineering judgement, not a measurement. Staged mode still exists (--rx-direct 0) and its contract runs on the model. The first accepted direct chunk is the test of NAT-040 item U5.

The engine comes up with a 512-byte placeholder destination so that the host collector sees the device before the receive path is installed; the companion (NAT-080) must treat that capacity as 'not ready'.

Timing rules checked by build.py: pet + 20 s <= 83 s (the unpetted hardware watchdog measured in NAT-075), 8 s <= return_after <= 63 s, deadline >= rx cap + return_after + 60 s and <= 600 s; built values rx cap 240 s, return_after 45 s, deadline 360 s, pet 30 s, report 10 s.

Two mutation passes were polluted by 'Disk quota exceeded' on the shared /tmp tmpfs (180 of 214 impl mutants of pass 2 were reported invalid for that reason); their C results are not used. Pass 5 ran with TMPDIR on the NVMe volume. Pass 4 found four build.py survivors (the RAMDISK_MAX literal and the size checks), killed by a test with the exact limits.

NAT-076's mutation pass had found two engine defects (a double ENDTRANSFER on a bus reset during a pending end; an idle XferComplete leaving the endpoint enabled with no transfer); this build uses the fixed engine.
established: Host-test: the hunks apply exactly once to the pinned sources and refuse a drifted base; the build and the NAT-044 package are reproducible from the recorded commands and the recorded hashes equal the files.

Host-test: the compiled receive phase behaves as listed in acceptance 2 under Unicorn and on the NAT-076 model, including the status codes 0-8, argument refusal, premature host traffic, a fault mid-stream, counters that disagree, a stalled stream and a 4 GiB window with the real-size reserve.
Host-test: 486 of 489 valid mutants of the new code, the hunk maker and the builder are killed; the other 3 are equivalent with reasons.
not_established: Anything about the S24: that the DWC3 DMA reaches the reserve above 4 GiB (NAT-040 item U5), the host-to-phone rate (the 225 s delivery budget needs about 11 MB/s), cache visibility of the delivered bytes to the kernel (a clean+invalidate over the reserve before receiving is the follow-up if the NAT-078 digest differs), watchdog behaviour while bulk is served (NAT-071), whether the payload kernel hands PID 1 stdio, how /dev/rmd1 behaves under read(2).
That the instruction-level model (Unicorn, no MMU, no caches, no real interrupt timing) and the NAT-076 DWC3 model are faithful to the Exynos 2400 controller.
That the image boots: the RECOVERY image was built and packaged, never written or run.

mutation_summary.final_pass: artifacts/nat-079/mutation-run5-full (docs/procedures/nat-079/mutation.json): 580 candidates, 91 invalid (51 do not parse, 40 fail the real build/fixture compile), 486 killed (3 by timeout), 3 survivors, all in equivalent.json

deviations_from_task_text: The task text names 'a staged-write self-test of the reserve before RX_BEGIN is accepted'. The built self-test is a CPU test of eight pages of the reserve (first, last and six interior pages: a pattern, its complement, then zero, with barriers) run before the destination is installed (a failure ends the phase with status 5 and installs no destination); a host that sent before that is refused. The receive itself is direct DMA by default, not staged, for the reason in the findings.

The reserve is the md1 reserve (2,475,720,704 B) in a 4096 MiB window (NAT-075 layout), registered as md1/rmd1 only; the root is never given to the kernel as md0 (md0 is the 16,635-byte NAT-077 probe, added through a new --ramdisk option of the builder).
The pinned NAT-074 sources are copied and patched; the NAT-076 engine files are compiled from docs/procedures/nat-076/engine/ and the build record lists them.
Mutation counts exclude 91 candidates that do not build (51 Python syntax errors in the build/hunk scripts, 40 C mutants rejected by zig -Werror or the fixture under cc -Wall -Wextra).
